plan.chase: The memo sits on my desk with seven seasons of Eric Taveras and one name next to his at second base. The 2041 line is the hinge — 54 homers in 555 at-bats, a rate of one every 10.3. The six seasons before it never got below 16.3, and 2036 was 31.4. The strikeout rate moved the other way: 81 in 2041, one every 6.9 at-bats, against a career band of 4.1 to 5.0. The peer, Sidney Tumolo, had 23 games and 88 at-bats, a tiny sample that makes the comparison almost useless for proving anything about Taveras. plan.focus: Whether Eric Taveras's 2041 power and strikeout rates represent a sustainable change or a single-season outlier, measured against his own six prior seasons and the thin peer sample.
plan.why: The memo's value is in the contrast: one season of 54 homers and 81 strikeouts against six seasons of 19-31 homers and 132-144 strikeouts. The strikeout rate dropping from 4.4 per at-bat to 6.9 is the more telling number, because power can fluctuate but contact skill is usually stable. If the A's are building around Taveras, they need to know which line is real.
checks: Confirm the 2041 season is complete and not a partial-year artifact.
Verify the strikeout rate calculation: 555 at-bats divided by 81 strikeouts equals 6.85, rounded to 6.9.
Check whether the 2041 ballpark or league context changed in a way that could explain the power spike.
Compare Taveras's 2041 batted-ball data, if available, to prior seasons for exit velocity or launch angle shifts.
Review the A's internal depth chart at second base to see if Tumolo's 23-game sample is being treated as a real alternative.
plan.interpretation: The numbers suggest two possible Taverases: the one who struck out every 4.1-5.0 at-bats and hit 19-31 homers, and the one who struck out every 6.9 at-bats and hit 54. The second version is better in every way that matters for a second baseman, but it exists in one season. The peer comparison is too small to anchor anything. The honest read is that 2041 is either a breakout or a career year, and the memo cannot tell which. The next season's strikeout rate is the tell.
